newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close higher on heavy turnover.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close higher on heavy turnover.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed slightly higher on Friday, holding steady above the strategic 13,200 level despite renewed fears on Wall Street of a hike in U.S. interest rates, brokers said.
"The market looks like it has stabilized," said Anthony Mak, associate director at Vickers Ballas. "But we could see it dip to 13,000 if there is further weakness on Wall Street."
The Hang Seng Index closed 19.35 points higher at 13,222.79 after a day of seesawing within a 100-point band. Turnover was a heavy HK$11.095 billion, well up on Thursday's HK$10.09 billion.
On Thursday, the Hang Seng index slid 248 points or 1.8 percent in the wake of Wall Street's 101-point drop on New Year's Eve.
Better-than-expected U.S. economic data on Thursday re-ignited inflation and interest rate hike fears, pushing the Dow down another 96 points before it rallied to end 5.78 points off at 6,442.49.
Trading in Hang Seng Index futures took on a positive tone in the afternoon with the January contract putting on 85 points to 13,215 but volume was low at 13,579 contracts.
Technically, the chart looks a little mixed, said Ted Chen, technical analyst at Technical Data Inc.
"Looking at the weekly chart, the Hang Seng looks like it is trying to find a bottom around the 13,000 level," said Chen.
At the close, the 10-day moving average at the 13,217 had just cut above the 20-day, a bullish short term signal, analysts said.
Market breadth remained positive. A total of 353 issued advanced, 288 declined and 322 were unchanged.
The chief feature on Friday was trading in CITIC Pacific which led the most active table. The share shed HK$2.50 or 5.54 percent to close at HK$42.60 on very heavy turnover of HK$827.87 million.

Other leading red chips were also hit by profit-taking. China Resources lost HK$0.45, or 2.47 percent, to HK$17.75 on heavy turnover of HK$319.32 million. Shanghai Industrial also shed HK$0.20 to HK$27.80.

H shares maintained their gains as the Hang Seng China Enterprise Index ended 1.97 percent higher at 1,059.05. Guangdong Kelon finished the day HK$0.40 higher at HK$6.00 after setting a new intraday high of HK$6.05.
Hang Seng Index heavyweights HSBC Holdings added HK$1.50 to close at HK$165.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties jumped HK$2.00, or 2.17 percent to HK$94.25
